gaps.fact: Rioja Alta is continental and Rioja Alavesa is the coolest and wettest of the three zones. Every chapter, stem and article line pairs Alta and Alavesa as the cooler west; none sets Alavesa apart as the coolest and wettest.

Rioja's three soils, calcareous clay, ferrous clay and alluvial. Chalky clay is taught for Alavesa; ferrous clay and alluvium stand only in the article and the Régionale map row, and no stem asks a Rioja soil.

Malvasía and Garnacha Blanca as white Rioja grapes. Malvasía is an article line only; Garnacha Blanca is never tied to Rioja anywhere (the article's grape list omits it although it counts nine authorised whites).

Some modern producers make fruit focused wines with French oak and avoid the traditional terms Crianza, Reserva and Gran Reserva. Only the article teaches the modern style and Artadi's exit; no chapter fact or stem.
Marqués de Cáceres and Finca Allende appear nowhere in the Codex; Marqués de Riscal and La Rioja Alta are never the key of a stem (only López de Heredia is asked, under Producers & Icons).

How oak use and oxidation in Rioja change the pairing: the long American oak and the oxidative note of a traditional Gran Reserva or an old white Rioja against a fruit led modern wine. Oak is taught generically for pairing; no stem or chapter fact ties Rioja's oak and oxidation to the dish.

courtUpdates.now: Unchanged in substance and now settled: the breakaway Viñedos de Álava DO, which had held transitional national protection since 2022 for Alavesa growers who wanted to leave the DOCa, was annulled by the Basque High Court on 5 November 2024; the Supreme Court refused the growers' appeal in June 2025 and the Basque government set aside its approving resolution of 2021 on 9 December 2025. Rioja Alavesa remains a zone of DOCa Rioja.

Beyond the map: Producers & Icons (i-xq5ngfnr, i-fk4kts5g), Classifications & Labels (c-4cysi1tp, c-35imqkzm, c-nzyna6l9), Service & Hospitality (c-wmsk4tor, decanting a Gran Reserva), Geography & Maps (i-kpw2z6di, i-y61faisq), Grapes & Labels (i-pzcv607m) and Food & Pairing (i-iy3or7h3, i-q12cyymq). Rioja is the best drilled Spanish subject: the ageing ladder with the bottle minimums, the zones and the 2018 rename, Viñedo Singular, carbonic Joven and the Bordeaux story all have stems, and every chapter, article and reference row gives Gran Reserva as sixty months with twenty four in cask and twenty four in bottle, which meets the Court's two years in oak. The Court's Cantabrian Mountains reach the Codex as the Sierra de Cantabria, the limestone ridge on Rioja's northern edge (a fair reading of the same rain shadow), but the Pyrenees, which the Court names in the Introductory physical feature cell, are never tied to Rioja. The thin cells are Alavesa's climate, the soils, Malvasía and Garnacha Blanca, the modern style, two producers and the pairing. Two searches spent: the Viñedos de Álava annulment (logged above, the Court's row stands) and the Consejo's recent changes, which touch no printed cell: the plenary of June 2025, approved by the ministry in October 2025, lets the specification protect wines up to a degree and a half below the old alcohol minimums, and the plenary of 24 July 2026 voted to drop the fifty barrique minimum for an ageing bodega, with the Crianza, Reserva and Gran Reserva times unchanged and the text still to enter the specification. Card, fact and trap numbers count from one.
